results.note: Live in all modes tested (-c, script file, stdin) and via eval and source. Every command after the first external command in a function/eval/source body running as a pipeline member is silently dropped, and the member's exit status is that command's (pipefail rc=0 instead of 1). Controls that clear in_pipeline still pass: { }|cat, ( )|cat, for-loop|cat all print 'A\nB' in both shells. Source locations unchanged at HEAD: strategies.py:605 `if context.in_pipeline:`; only subshell.py:82-83 and control_flow.py:91-92 save/clear it; function.py _function_frame (line 196) does not. NOTE: /bin/false does not exist on macOS (both shells report 'No such file or directory'), so the last repro was re-run with /usr/bin/false: bash prints B, psh prints nothing. Oracle 5.3.15 matches the report's 5.2.26 expectations exactly.

results.note: Live, -c mode, run from fresh temp dirs. In every mid-word case (after a double-quoted string, ${...} expansion, backtick cmdsub, and the {v} named-fd form) psh steals the trailing digit/{name} as an fd prefix and emits a redirect, while bash 5.3.15 treats it as word text and applies a plain '>' redirect (the file k3/k4/k5/g2 receives 'x2'/'a{v}'). Correction to bash53_output field: in bash, 'echo "x"2>k3; cat k3' prints 'x2' from cat (stdout of echo went to k3), and 'echo "x"2>k3; ls' prints only 'k3'; in psh 'echo "x"2>k3; ls' prints 'x\nk3' (x to stdout, k3 empty). operator.py:438 at HEAD still checks input_text[pos].isdigit() with no word-start check, and the '{' named-fd path at :446 likewise. The >& sub-item (lexer2:F1b) is also still present: WORD 'x2' [5:7) and REDIRECT_DUP '2>&1' [6:10) overlap, though for the unquoted 'echo x2>&1' case the runtime result coincidentally matches bash ('x2'); the ${u-x}2>&1 variant diverges ('x' vs 'x2').
